judgements.reason: Section 6's 'matched' sentence is in tension with Table 1's 16/120 and 17/120 committee captures versus 0/120 for the gated majority and Finding 2's statement that committees add no safety on this task.
Section 3.3's G3 formula is committee approval, while Table 1 prints 21.8 for hybrid without marking it committee-only even though hybrid release also requires a majority gate.
Section 3.4 does not state whether committee auditors see the fifty-reviewer board or can be run without it, so the 7-versus-50 call count does not establish token, dollar, or latency equivalence.
The manuscript discloses 60 paired committee draws but gives no seed map or draw-level uncertainty for regime comparisons across shares.

Sections 1 and 6 use size-independent language while Section 3.2 limits verification to a bounded world and Section 5 lists honest-error independence under the guarantee although it is only a G3 assumption.
Appendix B.1 checks one case, so a missing case_id predicate that leaks attestations across cases would be outside the checked state space despite G1's per-case binding claim.
The abstract's 1.9-2.8x length signal omits Section 4.3's admission that colluders received a longer conflicting prompt and that hidden reasoning is included.
Section 2's novelty gap relies on 2026 references and the References section still contains a note to verify every reference before submission.
Appendix B.4's shared-minority feature requires colluders to be on the losing side, and Section 4.3 reports only one anecdotal zero-collusion false cluster rather than a denominator.
Section 4.3's text says errors were too rare to affect any committee, but its near-miss table reports 1-of-1 committees captured by honest error alone in 2/108 DeepSeek trials.

Table 1's nonmonotonic seat bounds and captures across 1-of-1, 3-of-5, and 4-of-7, together with the caption's 60 independent draws, show that cross-row comparisons need seating uncertainty treatment.
The abstract's 23,376-state confirmation omits Section 3.2 and Appendix B.1's one-case, three-seat, depth-6 bound, which cannot rule out cross-case SQLite isolation bugs.
Section 4.3 acknowledges the longer colluder prompt, and Section 3.4's non-target honest-voting cases provide logged material for a within-prompt length control.
Section 3.4 specifies visible/hidden information for voters but not whether seated auditors see the board or when audits occur, leaving the committee-only cost comparison underspecified.
The detector's shared-minority rule in Appendix B.4 presumes colluders remain a voting minority, and Section 4.3 does not quantify zero-collusion false-positive runs.
The References section retains an editorial verification instruction and lists several 2026 arXiv identifiers whose status is not established in the manuscript.
Table 1's unlabeled hybrid 21.8, Section 6's matched-judgment sentence, and the abstract's omission of the symmetric-HMAC architectural caveat are all supported by the manuscript's own disclosures.
Table 1 shows committee unsafe releases while gated majority has zero, so Section 6's matched judgment claim exceeds the exact-match evidence and Finding 2's cost-capture framing.
The checked world in Section 3.2 and Appendix B.1 is smaller than the live 24-case, seven-seat regimes, and the abstract's confirmation sentence does not state that bound.
Finding 1 says voters could not verify symmetric HMACs, so the abstract's 48/48 forgery bullet needs the by-construction caveat.
The abstract presents the output-length ratio as a monitoring signal while Section 4.3 states it is confounded by a longer colluder prompt and hidden reasoning.

Finding 2's 12-versus-18 capturable draw and Table 1's nonmonotonic bounds show cross-regime differences can reflect seating draws, but the manuscript does not flag this in the table or figure caption.
Section 2's gap claim rests on an incomplete scan and unverified 2026 candidates, and the References section still contains the verification note.
The hybrid row copies the committee-only G3 expectation while hybrid release also requires majority approval, which is empirically zero under the tested honest-error and colluder-share conditions.

Sections 1 and 6 state size-independent guarantees, but Section 3.2 provides only bounded checking and Section 5 conflates G3's independence assumption with the guarantee; at-most-once is only shown as a SQLite transaction.
Section 3.4 does not specify auditors' board exposure or whether committee-only deployment omits the fifty-reviewer stage, so the sevenfold cost claim needs clarification.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The manuscript pools 120 target trials from 60 independent committee draws and paired board conditions, but it provides no draw-level uncertainty estimates and some cross-regime comparisons appear driven by only 12 seating draws per share.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Report denominators and seed structure clearly, provide cluster-robust, exact binomial, or bootstrap intervals keyed to independent draws, and either resample logged decisions or explicitly label nonmonotonic cross-regime differences as seating-sample artifacts.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Finding 2 reconciles the 24 versus 36 figures, but Table 1 and Section 3.3 still do not give an explicit formula translating independent draws, paired board conditions, shares, and compliance into the reported G2 and G3 numbers.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short formula or table showing how seat bounds and expectations are computed from 12 independent draws per share doubled across paired conditions, including compliance-adjusted expectations.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Honest unsafe error is near zero, so G3's independence assumption and the committee safety case under honest judgment error remain untested, although this does not undermine G1 or G2.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Scope committee-safety claims in the abstract and conclusion to exact-match or mechanically checkable tasks, keep G3 labeled untested, and propose a judgment task or injected-error calibration.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The direct-majority forgery failure is architectural because voters lack symmetric-HMAC verification, and while the gated-majority baseline is the informative control, the abstract and conclusion can still overread the baseline failure.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Add the by-construction caveat and gated-majority numbers to the abstract, state the majority/tie rule, and present public-key or tool-assisted voting as future work rather than implying a general voting failure.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Bounded verification covers one case, three seats, quorum 2, depth 6, and a same-team specification, so it does not cover live 7-seat regimes, 24 cases, or cross-case isolation bugs such as missing case_id filters.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: State the verification bound in the abstract, add a two-case bounded check or cross-case mutant, or provide an explicit argument why omitted dimensions cannot affect S1-S4, and release the specification and mutants.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The output-length association is confounded by the longer colluder prompt and hidden reasoning, and the abstract presents it as a monitoring signal without that caveat.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Qualify the abstract, compare colluder versus honest length on non-target cases where the prompt is shared, and avoid describing the association as a measured cost of deception.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The detector demonstrates recovery of the planted signature, but its shared-minority feature assumes colluders remain a voting minority and the zero-collusion false-positive denominator is not reported.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Limit the claim to the planted signature, state the less-than-50%-capture assumption, and report false-positive clusters over all zero-collusion runs by model and condition.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The References section retains an editorial verification note and several 2026 arXiv identifiers underpinning the novelty gap are not verifiable from the manuscript.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Verify all identifiers and titles, remove the leftover editorial note, and qualify the novelty gap as provisional if any cited works remain inaccessible.

revised_own_concerns.issue: Table 1's hybrid a-priori G3 value of 21.8 is a committee-only opportunity estimate, not a hybrid release expectation, because hybrid release also requires majority approval and the dependence between committee members and voters is not modeled.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Label 21.8 as committee-only or not applicable for hybrid release, or compute a joint majority-and-committee expectation with the dependence and tie rule stated.

revised_own_concerns.issue: The sevenfold cost comparison is expressed in model calls, but the manuscript does not specify the committee auditors' information set or whether tokens, dollars, latency, and the fifty-reviewer stage scale similarly.
revised_own_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify whether committee-only deployment omits the reviewer stage, specify auditor prompts and board exposure, and report token or dollar costs or consistently describe the result as fewer model requests.

new_concerns.issue: Section 4.3 states that near-miss errors were too rare to affect any committee, but the same section's table reports 1-of-1 committees captured by honest error alone in 2/108 DeepSeek trials.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify whether the statement applies only to committees larger than 1-of-1, correct the wording, and specify the configurations underlying the mixed-model null result.

new_concerns.issue: Sections 1 and 6 claim size-independent oversight and at-most-once release, but the evidence is bounded checking of a SQLite transaction and does not demonstrate external gateway side effects or arbitrary-scale deployment.
new_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a G1-G3 scope table, define release as the database transition unless external-action semantics were tested, and make size-independent assurance conditional on verifying the invariants beyond the checked bound.

rebuttals.response: I concede the 24/36 counts are reconcilable via Finding 2's 12/18 independent draws doubled across paired conditions; I have downgraded my concern to requesting an explicit formula rather than claiming irreconcilability.
I concede that Finding 2 reconciles the 24 versus 36 values; my remaining request is only an explicit table or formula so readers can verify the units without reconstructing the pairing.
I agree that honest-error independence is only an assumption of G3, not G1 or G2, and I revised my concern to target committee safety under judgment tasks rather than the mechanical guarantees.
I concede the gated-majority baseline already provides a crowd-plus-mechanical-check comparison; my remaining concern is the abstract/conclusion framing and the untested public-key/tool baseline.
I agree Finding 1 already labels the forgery result architectural, so I keep this as a minor abstract-overclaim issue rather than a major missing control.
I concede the manuscript already limits detection to the planted signature; I retain only the narrower request for a false-positive denominator and the minority-voting assumption.
I concede the herding null is already qualified in Section 4.3 and Appendix A, so I withdrew the overclaim concern; exact intervals are optional.
I concede the manuscript does not make a strong herding-absence claim because it labels the evidence weak and task-specific, so C8 remains withdrawn.
